S53.02.needs: none; a skill installed in .agiworkforce/skills/ or ~/.agiworkforce/skills/ helps
S53.02.note: The list comes back empty if the account's plan lacks the Skills capability (tier_cache check in apps/cli/src/skills.rs discover_skills); I did not verify which plans have it.
steps: Start the CLI and open the chat.
Type /skills and press Enter.
Compare the list with Expected: each skill shows its name, a description and a [project] or [global] tag, or a 'No skills found.' message when none are installed.
S53.02.where: /skills (type it in the chat and press Enter)

labels.text: Usage: /skills import <path to SKILL.md or its folder>

S53.03.needs: a skill folder with SKILL.md on disk
S53.03.note: Personal skills live in the user's config folder (~/.agiworkforce/skills, or AGIWORKFORCE_HOME). I found no owner or sharing field in the code, so 'only they have' is not visible in the UI. /create-skill writes to the project folder, not the personal folder.
steps: Make a folder with a SKILL.md file on your computer, and note its path.
Type /skills import followed by that path, then press Enter.
Read the 'Imported the skill to' message, then type /skills and check the skill is listed with the [global] tag.
S53.03.where: /skills import <path to SKILL.md or its folder> (type it in the chat), then /skills

S53.04.needs: a project folder with its own .agiworkforce/skills skill
S53.04.note: Project skills load only after consent, and the prompt appears again when a project skill changes. The earlier quoted line at skills.rs:190 was not found, but project scoping and the consent prompt are present (skills.rs around lines 169 and 426-475).
steps: Open a terminal in a project folder that has a .agiworkforce/skills folder with a skill in it.
Start the CLI there. When asked whether to load the project's skills, read the prompt and answer yes.
Type /skills and press Enter.
Check the project skill is listed with the [project] tag. Start the CLI in another folder and check it is not listed.
S53.04.where: Start the CLI in a project folder that contains .agiworkforce/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, answer the prompt, then type /skills

steps: Install or add at least one skill with a name and a description.
Type /skills and press Enter.
Check each row shows the skill name, then its description (or '(no description)' if empty).
S53.07.where: /skills (type it in the chat and press Enter)

S53.08.note: I searched apps/cli for invocation hint text (help, hints, 'Use /', 'type /' near skill) in tui_app.rs, widgets and repl and found no user-visible text that explains how a skill is invoked. The only skill-invocation strings are model-facing (skills.rs 'Skill bodies are lazy-loaded') and the /skills empty-state text, which names folders only. Invocation works by /<skill name> (skills.rs skill_command_prompt).

labels.text: Files this skill bundles (scripts/, references/, assets/) are under

S53.10.needs: a skill folder with SKILL.md and references/ on disk, in the <id>/SKILL.md layout
S53.10.note: The bundle path note is added only for the <id>/SKILL.md package layout (tree_hash present). Whether the model actually reads the file is decided by the model, so the check is the answer.
steps: Make a skill folder with SKILL.md and a references/ subfolder holding a note file with a made-up fact, for example a code word.
Start the CLI, make sure the skill is listed by /skills.
Type /<skill name> and a request that needs the note, then press Enter.
Check the answer uses the fact from the reference file. The skill result text tells the model where the bundled files are.
S53.10.where: /<skill name> <request> (type the skill's name with a slash in the chat and press Enter)

labels.text: Files this skill bundles (scripts/, references/, assets/) are under

S53.11.needs: a skill folder with a script, and the tool that runs commands allowed in the session
S53.11.note: No code in apps/cli/src/skills.rs runs scripts. The skill result only names the folder and the model decides whether to run a script through its own tools, so the run is not guaranteed.
steps: Make a skill folder with SKILL.md and a scripts/ subfolder holding a script that writes a made-up word to a file, and have SKILL.md tell the model to run it.
Invoke the skill with /<skill name> and a request, then watch the chat for a shell command run.
Check the file the script writes exists afterwards.
S53.11.where: Effect is inside the skill run after /<skill name> <request>; no control of its own

S53.14.needs: a skill file with a tools: line naming a missing tool
S53.14.note: The check uses the built-in tool list only (skills.rs skill_command_prompt). /skills does not show required tools.
steps: Make a skill whose SKILL.md frontmatter lists a tool name the CLI does not have, for example tools: [no-such-tool].
Start the CLI and type /<skill name> with any request, then press Enter.
Check the message says the skill cannot be loaded and names the missing tool, instead of running the skill.
S53.14.where: /<skill name> <request> (type it in the chat and press Enter)

labels.text: Apply this skill to the current work.

S53.17.note: Typing /<skill name> works in both the chat screen and the line REPL (command_registry.rs expand_dynamic_slash_invocation).
steps: In the chat, type / and look for the skill's name in the list that opens.
Pick the skill and type a request after it, then press Enter.
Check the answer follows the skill's steps; the model is told 'The user invoked the /<name> skill.'
S53.17.where: / then pick the skill's name, then type a request (in the chat)

labels.text: Skill metadata loaded from consented locations.

S53.18.needs: an installed skill with a clear description
S53.18.note: No code outside tests calls match_skills_scored or extract_skill_mentions, so there is no code-scored automatic match; the model chooses from the catalog in the system prompt. $name and @name mentions are parsed only by tests.
steps: Install a skill whose description states a clear use, for example 'Use when the user asks for a haiku'.
Start the CLI and type a request that matches that description, without naming the skill or using a slash.
Check whether the answer follows the skill, or the transcript shows a call to the skill tool.
S53.18.where: Effect is in the chat: an ordinary request with no slash command

labels.text: ↑↓ navigate   Space toggle   Enter save   Esc cancel

S53.20.note: /skills-toggle exists only in the full-screen chat; the line REPL has no such command.
steps: Type /skills-toggle and press Enter.
Move with the arrow keys to a skill, press Space to turn it off, then press Enter to save.
Type /skills and check the skill is no longer listed; the skill folder is still on disk.
Type /skills-toggle again, press Space on the same skill to turn it on, press Enter, and check /skills lists it again.
S53.20.where: /skills-toggle (type it in the full-screen chat, which opens an overlay)

S53.21.needs: a skill folder or SKILL.md file on disk
S53.21.note: There is no file picker. The import takes a typed path and copies the skill into the user's skills folder (skills.rs import_skill).
steps: Make a skill folder with a SKILL.md file on your computer, and note its path.
Type /skills import and that path, then press Enter.
Read the 'Imported the skill to' message, then type /skills and check the skill is listed.
Invoke it with /<skill name> and a request, and check the answer uses the skill.
S53.21.where: /skills import <path to SKILL.md or its folder> (type it in the chat and press Enter)
